---
title: Differentiability
---

A Laplace approximation is a function of the parameters it is fitted at. Its
curvature, its log marginal likelihood and its predictive all depend on
$\theta$, and some uses need that gradient. Marginal-likelihood training of
the network (Immer et al., 2021)[^immer2021] differentiates the log marginal
likelihood with respect to $\theta$. So **laplacekit** keeps two modes apart.

## The front door detaches

`lk.laplace` fits for the user, who wants numbers. It detaches the chosen
parameters, runs the fit loop under `torch.no_grad`, detaches the result,
and gives the posterior its own copy of the mean. Nothing it returns is attached
to the user's autograd graph, and training the module afterwards doesn't move
the posterior.

## By hand, the curvature stays differentiable

The steps that `lk.laplace` composes don't detach the params. The curvature
part of the statistic, the operator, the posterior and its mean keep their
graph to `params`, and so do the log-determinant and prior terms of
`neg_log_marglik`. The one exception is the data-fit term. The fold computes
the log-likelihood under `no_grad`, so `stat.data_fit` is a value. For the
gradient of the whole objective, we add the log-likelihood back from a forward
of our own, which leaves the objective's value as it is:

```python
params = lk.subsets.last_layer(fn, caps)
fit = lk.core.fit_curvature(fn, lik, params, lk.DenseGGN(), capabilities=caps)
stat = fit.update(fit.init(), batch)
post = fit.posterior(fit.finalize(stat), prior=prior, n_data=stat.count)

log_lik = lk.core.log_prob(lik, fn(params, batch.inputs), batch.targets).sum()
post = copy.replace(post, data_fit=(stat.data_fit,))
loss = lk.objectives.neg_log_marglik(post) + stat.data_fit - log_lik
grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, list(params.values()))
```

Without the last two terms, `grads` would miss the gradient of the
log-likelihood. [Step by step](../examples/by_hand.py#gradients) runs this on
a real model.

## What a plugin must do

A plugin's code runs in both modes, so it must not choose for the user. In
`update`, `finalize`, a prior's `log_prob`, a predictive or an objective:

- no `.detach()`, `torch.no_grad()` or `.item()` on anything that depends on
  the params or on a hyperparameter;
- no round trip through NumPy or Python floats in the math.

The front door's `no_grad` turns all of it into plain tensor arithmetic
anyway, so this costs nothing there. Tensors that never depend on the params
(sign vectors, masks, counts) are fine as they are.

Objectives have one more rule. `lk.Minimize` minimizes them over the logs of
the hyperparameters with L-BFGS, so they must be differentiable in them.
`lk.testing.check_objective` checks that a finite gradient reaches every
hyperparameter of the posterior, and the [Tuning objectives](objective.py) guide shows one whose
gradient flows through `lk.predict`.

[^immer2021]: Immer, A., Bauer, M., Fortuin, V., Rätsch, G., & Khan, M. E. (2021). Scalable marginal likelihood estimation for model selection in deep learning. *ICML*. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04975>
